label: D1 surge after an unrewarded visit to S1; S1/a1 history lifts GO and D2
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == -1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase != D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_state == 1)
explanation: Raw GRU candidate n of unit 4 (normally near -0.7, rising slowly over the episode in the timing baseline). The dominant driver is at D1: when the previous trial reached S1 and was unrewarded (a1 S1 u or a2 S1 u) the value jumps by about +0.9 (residual about +0.8 to +0.9, often to positive values). A second D1 term covers unrewarded D1s where the previous state lies outside the window (+0.47, a window artifact; the agent did observe that state). D1 after a rewarded S2 visit is slightly lower (-0.12). At GO it is higher when the previous state was S1 (+0.19). At GO and D2 an unrewarded previous trial adds +0.08. At D2 it is higher when this trial reached S1 (+0.14, observed at D2) and when the previous choice was a1 (+0.12) or the previous state was S1 (+0.05). So the unit codes S1 not rewarded / a switch away from S1, mostly at D1. All terms are observed; no future or hidden variables are used. Value, hidden good state and since_rev add little (reference scores 0.03, 0.06, 0.00). Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.74; last-trial table reference 0.70; all ceiling 0.81.

issues: I reproduced the reported score exactly: test R^2 beyond timing is 0.7345, against 0.70 for the last-trial table and a 0.81 ceiling. The central claim holds. In the profile residuals, D1 after a1 S1 u is +0.87 and after a2 S1 u is +0.78, while every other previous-trial pattern sits between -0.25 and -0.02. The first term alone scores 0.47 on test, and adding the window-edge term brings it to 0.52.

The D1 surge is not a fixed step. It builds up over consecutive unrewarded trials. The worst-fit windows are all D1 steps after a run of losses, where the actual value is about 0.66-0.80 but the prediction is only 0.02-0.18. Adding (phase==D1)*(prev_state==1)*(prev_reward==0)*(tv('reward',-2)==0) gets a weight of +0.34 and raises test R^2 from about 0.734 to 0.747. The label does not mention this.

The D2 claim 'higher when this trial reached S1' is really a conjunction of choice and state, a1 common to S1. The profile residuals by this trial's choice x state at D2 are a1S1 +0.22, a1S2 +0.02, a2S1 -0.09 and a2S2 -0.16. When (phase==D2)*(action==1)*(state==1) is added, the weight on the plain state==1 term drops from 0.14 to about 0.00 and the conjunction gets +0.26.

Two of the original terms add almost nothing: (phase==D2)*(prev_state==1) at +0.05 and (phase==D1)*S2-rewarded at -0.12. The window-edge term (+0.47) comes from where the window is cut, not from the agent. The explanation does say this openly.

The remaining misses are modest and scattered across small cells, at most about 0.16. With the original terms they are D2 after a1 S2 r (-0.16), D2 after a2 S2 u (-0.12) and D1 after a2 S2 u (+0.11). The improved terms leave them almost unchanged. I found no large systematic error class.

No future variables are used, so no observed-only check was needed. My improved term set reaches 0.772 test, which is 95% of the 0.81 ceiling, so the original explanation was close but missed the two refinements above.
